module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: Within any successful finite grant lifecycle, accepted transitions preserve exact record identity, non-authority, observation/effect accounting, live-grant ceiling/epoch/revocation safety, approval/dispatch custody, and recursive trace validity; event batches compose, revoked IDs persist, no successful suffix can approve, dispatch, or commit an effect under an already revoked ID, rejected events have no successor, and accepted rollback clears exact effect accounting.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Exact numeric grant, principal, operation, target, ceiling, epoch, logical time, expiry, remaining uses, approval, dispatch, revocation, local effect, observation, and rollback fields across seven event kinds, an inductive state invariant, a recursive trace-validity predicate, and three reachable traces covering one-use, two-use, and revocation lifecycles.
assumptions: Grant, identity, target ownership, time, epoch, approval, dispatch, effect, observation, revocation, and rollback fields are truthful and authentic inputs.
One sequential finite state machine is sufficient for the checked cases; concurrency, distributed revocation, partial observation, descendant effects, and external compensation are omitted.
The local public-safe effect and exact fixture rollback do not represent production authorization, security, or effect-complete recovery.
countermodels: Authority above the caller ceiling and confused-deputy principal substitution are rejected.
Expired, stale-epoch, and revoked grants cannot dispatch.
Effect without dispatch, observation overcount, premature rollback, post-revocation effect or reissuance, and reuse of a consumed one-shot grant are rejected.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: The independently implemented consumer binds six authority fixtures, three reachable traces with twenty events, twenty invariant prefixes, twenty-three exact batch compositions, nine governed repository scenarios, one local effect, one independent observation, one exact rollback, two pre-effect denials, and five revocation records while rejecting 50/50 source/model mutations with exact rejected-state preservation.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Adequate for arbitrary-length but finite sequential grant, approval, dispatch, local effect, observation, revocation, bounded-use, rollback, trace-composition, and rejection-noninterference consequences. It does not establish authentic identities or receipts, wise grants, complete observation, concurrent or distributed revocation, deployed enforcement, effect-complete recovery, production security, safety, transfer, or support movement.

module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: Finite replacement records route missing qualification, identity, fresh evidence, evaluator separation, regression floors, canary and monitor custody, rollback handles and dry runs, irreversible-effect and residual ownership, deprecation, retirement, non-claim, or approval fields away from default commit; a reachable lifecycle preserves identity, non-authority, and authority ceilings across arbitrary accepted runs, blocks default after monitor failure, restores the prior implementation on rollback, and retains three bounded fixture bridges.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Commit predicates, seven transaction routes, twelve lifecycle routes, a seven-stage preparation/canary/monitor/default-or-rollback transition model, immutable field/prior/candidate/ceiling identity, authority and receipt accounting, plus trace, identity-sequence, and intent-governed summary fixtures.
assumptions: All field identities, qualification, evaluator, regression, canary, monitor, rollback, effect, residual, approval, and non-claim records are truthful and complete for the declared inventory.
The hand-authored route order and Boolean fields adequately represent the bounded replacement decision; hidden state, concurrency, and unregistered descendants are omitted.
A fixture rollback handle, monitor status, or restored prior identifier does not establish semantic recovery, useful improvement, production rollback, or reversal of external effects.
countermodels: Authority widening without governance and a captured evaluator route to review instead of default commit.
Failed regression, failed canary, or a monitor incident routes to quarantine, canary-only, or rollback rather than promotion.
Missing rollback, irreversible-effect owner, residual owner, deprecation notice, retirement receipt, non-claim boundary, or approval blocks terminal defaulting in the corresponding model.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: The recompiling trace consumer binds the exact 52-theorem surface, checks two valid transactions, three rejecting controls, four identity-sequence controls, a monitor-triggered rollback, and no-promotion boundary; the transaction harness accepts five and rejects nine fixtures, and the intent-governed bridge checks two valid and six expected-invalid traces.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Adequate for the declared finite transaction/lifecycle routes, arbitrary-run sequential custody and composition, exact modeled rollback restoration, and three deterministic bridge summaries. It does not establish useful replacement, field or inventory completeness, evaluator or monitor validity, semantic or effect-complete recovery, irreversible-effect reversal, deployed canary behavior, production rollback, safety, transfer, or support movement.

module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: Under hand-authored finite predicates, generic review, delegation, and accountability failures route explicitly; a versioned correction-control lifecycle additionally orders material notice, independent review, bounded control, affected-party-representative challenge, and accountable correction while preserving exact custody, non-authority, and a non-increasing authority ceiling.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Two small decision records and their generic routes plus a six-stage correction-control state machine with exact action, affected-party, principal, reviewer, controller, version, expiry, authority, correction-path, challenge, accountability, residual, support, and external-effect fields; one five-event witness reaches correction and seven closed substitutions reject.
assumptions: High-impact, review usability, delegation bounds, denial, accountability, appeal, interruption, and rollback fields are truthful authored predicates.
The route and lifecycle fields truthfully encode the represented notice, correction paths, review independence, affected-party representation, expiry, accountability, and residual facts.
A successful authored transition does not demonstrate comprehension, standing, consent quality, reviewer competence, deployed rollback, shutdown, or effective correction.
countermodels: A high-impact record with missing pre-effect review must select the review route under the assumed predicate.
A low-risk record with unbounded delegation must select narrowing under the assumed predicate.
A denied record without an accountable principal must select the audit-residual route under the assumed predicate.
Missing notice, self-review, unbounded delegation, authority widening, outsider challenge, missing accountability, and consent laundering cannot enter the accepted lifecycle.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: The four generic declarations remain bounded route consequences. Twenty lifecycle theorems add exact accepted advancement, custody, non-authority, narrowing, phase obligations, arbitrary-run preservation, composition, one complete five-event witness, and seven closed substitutions; the independent agency-rights validator recompiles the exact surface and reconstructs all accepted and rejected lifecycle cases.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Adequate for the declared finite route implications and versioned correction-control lifecycle ordering, custody, non-authority, narrowing, witness, and refusal consequences. It does not establish corrigibility, shutdown incentives, notice comprehension, affected-party standing, consent quality, reviewer competence, usable correction, successful correction, rollback execution, embedded-agent behavior, safety, deployment, transfer, or support movement.

module_dispositions.plain_language_proposition: A finite vertical can move from one exact root intent through command, plan, job, approval, dispatch, attempted and observed local effect, artifact binding, independent-verification receipt, and delivery only while parent identity and authority ceilings remain intact; missing approval, hidden override, authority widening, effect without dispatch, and delivery without verification are rejected.
module_dispositions.modeled_state: Fifteen layer states, fourteen event kinds, root and artifact identities, authority ceiling, approval and dispatch custody, attempted and observed effect counts, artifact binding, verification, delivery, residual, stop, rollback and quarantine fields, plus one ten-event delivered trace.
assumptions: Intent, artifact, authority, approval, dispatch, observation, verifier, delivery, residual, rollback, and quarantine fields are truthful and exactly identified.
The finite vertical and event order are sufficient for the checked local scenarios; natural-language meaning, partial effects, concurrency, external descendants, and asynchronous failure are omitted.
An independentVerifier Boolean and observed-effect count do not establish evaluator independence, complete effect observation, useful delivery, or production execution.
countermodels: Missing approval blocks authorization and authority above the root ceiling is rejected.
A hidden override or effect attempt without a prior dispatch receipt is rejected.
Delivery without a prior independent-verification receipt is rejected.
module_dispositions.mutation_evidence: The independent vertical consumer checks nine scenarios, eighty-nine events, six local effects, exact schema/result identity, and thirty rejected mutations; the older handoff consumer separately preserves its deterministic source-to-delivery boundary.
module_dispositions.maximum_inference: Adequate for exact finite root/parent joins, non-widening authority, approval/dispatch custody, local effect observation, artifact binding, verification, delivery, and encoded rejection routes. It does not establish intent fidelity, parser correctness, authentic authority or receipts, prompt-injection resistance, complete effects, verifier independence, useful delivery, deployment, transfer, or support movement.

cluster_maximum_inference: The cluster is adequate for its recorded finite sequential authority/effect lifecycle, replacement transaction routes and bridge summaries, corrigibility route and correction-control lifecycle consequences, and intent-to-local-effect vertical. It proves no identity or receipt authentic, no grant wise, no notice comprehended, no standing legitimate, no monitor, reviewer, or verifier valid, no inventory complete, no external effect reversed, no system corrigible, no intent preserved in meaning, and no empirical, safety, deployment, transfer, SOTA, AGI, ASI, support, release, or publication claim.
